LUSAIL, Qatar, Nov 7 : Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi grabbed pole position for the Qatar Grand Prix on Saturday, smashing the lap record twice to snatch pole from Ducati's MotoGP championship leader Marc Marquez.
Bezzecchi clocked one minute 50.028 seconds at the Lusail International Circuit to take pole, 0.266 seconds ahead of Marquez while 2023 race winner Fabio di Giannantonio of VR46 Racing joins them on the front row after going third fastest.
"I made a mistake in the last corner, I tried a little bit too much. But I can't complain at all," Bezzecchi said.
"Perfect qualifying. I wanted to start in the front row and the pole position is even better. So, very happy."

Aprilia's Jorge Martin, who is second in the championship and 44 points behind Marquez, was left frustrated as he could go only 11th fastest - more than a second slower than his team mate.
Marquez can be crowned champion in Qatar if he finishes 30 points ahead of Martin and eight points ahead of Bezzecchi after Sunday's race.
"It was the main target as I said yesterday, the front row. It was not easy," Marquez said.
"We know that Marco has another pace this weekend. He's super fast. We must understand this and try to do our best."
Marquez's teammate Francesco Bagnaia was fifth fastest and he will be sandwiched between the two Trackhouse riders Raul Fernandez and Ai Ogura.
The Yamaha factory team and its satellite team Prima Pramac did not fly to Qatar after withdrawing from the Grand Prix citing "company-wide travel restrictions" in the region due to the war against Iran, leaving only 18 riders on the grid.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Nov 7 : A month after bidding farewell to tennis as a player, Gael Monfils has joined France's Davis Cup team as their captain, the French Tennis Federation (FFT) announced on Saturday.
Former world number six Monfils officially retired last month after bowing out in the US Open's second round in September, ending a 22-year professional career that included two Grand Slam semi-final appearances.
But Monfils is set to be at the courtside when France begin their Davis Cup qualifying campaign in February, after he took over the captaincy from Paul-Henri Mathieu, who led them to the quarter-finals last year.
“I am immensely proud to become captain of the French team. This blue jersey means so much to me,” Monfils said in a statement.

The 40-year-old represented France in eight editions of the Davis Cup, and won 12 of his 15 singles matches. He delivered one of his best performances in the 2014 final, beating Roger Federer in straight sets, although France lost the tie to Switzerland.
Monfils was not in the team when France won their 10th Davis Cup title in 2017, but said he was keen to add to their trophy cabinet as captain, a non-playing role.
"I want to build a genuine team-based project and create the momentum that will enable us to win titles together," he added.

Nov 7 : India beat New Zealand by four runs via the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method in a rain-hit one-day international on Saturday to take a 2-0 lead in the five-match series after a pace-dominated contest.
Put in to bat, New Zealand struggled to gain any momentum in Wellington as India's pace attack dismantled the batting line-up and restricted the hosts to 134 in 41 overs, with the match reduced to 47 overs per side due to rain.
India stumbled early in the chase but Shreyas Iyer and KL Rahul combined to wrest back control before rain halted play with the visitors on 113-7 and needing a further 22 runs for victory.
New Zealand's seamers, however, made India work hard for victory, turning what appeared to be a routine chase into a gripping, low-scoring contest.

Jacob Duffy struck with his first ball of the innings to dismiss India captain Shubman Gill for a golden duck before removing veteran Virat Kohli in his next over.
Rohit Sharma provided early momentum but Kyle Jamieson's disciplined spell left India wobbling at 47-4 and revived New Zealand's hopes of a comeback.
Iyer's 30 off 46 helped to steady the chase, while Rahul stood firm as wickets tumbled around him and anchored the chase with an unbeaten 26 off 38 balls, including two fours and two sixes, before rain cut short the contest.
"I thought it'll be an easy target but it wasn't," Gill said. "The pitch was challenging and we lost two extra wickets than we'd have liked... but happy we got there in the end."
The hosts had earlier left themselves with little margin for error after India's pacers ripped through the top order.
Auqib Nabi put New Zealand on the back foot with two early strikes, removing openers Tim Seifert and Will Young. Seifert's dismissal also marked the right-armer's maiden international wicket.
The hosts were reeling at 53-3 when Gurnoor Brar tightened India's grip with a double-wicket maiden, removing Tom Latham and the in-form Glenn Phillips.
Daryl Mitchell offered the only meaningful resistance for New Zealand, scoring 55 off 104 balls after earning a reprieve on 21 when Gill spilled a straightforward chance at cover, while captain Mitchell Santner chipped in with 31 off 38.
"It was a tricky wicket, there was no hiding," Santner said. "It was one of those wickets where the seamers were posing a challenge. It was a tough wicket but we could've scraped to 160-180."
Brar was named player of the match with figures of 4-30, while Nabi, Anshul Kamboj and Axar Patel claimed two wickets apiece.
The five-match series moves to Hamilton on Tuesday.

Astronomers spot white dwarf star with two rings of planetary debris

Artist's impression shows two gaseous discs of debris from planetary wreckage around the white dwarf J1328−1450 –– the dead core of a star similar to our sun that expelled its outer layers at the end of its lifetime. The star was suspected to have had a planetary system that was vaporized to rubble as the star died, and this debris ended up arranged in a disc arrangement like the one shown here, in this handout image released by the European Southern Observatory on October 27, 2026. ESO/L. Calcada/Handout via REUTERS

WASHINGTON, Nov 7 : Billions of years from now, the sun is expected to run out of fuel and greatly expand into what is called a red giant, eventually shedding its outer layers and leaving behind its dense core, a white dwarf. Some of the planets in our solar system would be destroyed while others might survive.
Researchers have now spotted a white dwarf with planetary debris swirling around it in an unusual configuration that may offer a peek into one possible outcome for our solar system in the distant future.
Unlike in similar systems previously observed, the debris disc surrounding this white dwarf appears to consist of two distinct rings. The researchers said the disc may have been shaped by two planetary or smaller rocky bodies that are embedded in the rings after managing to survive the star's violent death throes.
The white dwarf, named J1328−1450, is located in the Milky Way roughly 1,600 light-years from Earth, in the constellation Virgo. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year, 5.9 trillion miles (9.5 trillion km). The observations were made using the European Southern Observatory's Chile-based Very Large Telescope.

Prior to this discovery, astronomers had identified 21 white dwarfs with debris surrounding them, all of which had a single disc and not a double ring of material as the new observations reveal.
"It shows that the remnants of a planetary system can have a much more complex structure than we previously thought, and provides further support to the idea that planetary rocky bodies may survive the transformation of a star into a white dwarf," said astronomer Felipe Lagos-Vilches of Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María in Chile, one of the authors of the study published in the journal Nature Astronomy.
The white dwarf has a mass about 47 per cent that of the sun, jam-packed into a diameter roughly the same as that of Earth.
The surviving planetary bodies may be remnants of larger and heavily disrupted planets. One of them may be around the size of the dwarf planet Pluto, with the other one smaller than that.
Lagos-Vilches said the original star may have hosted a planetary system before it expanded dramatically into a red giant, engulfing some of the innermost planets while ones with more distant orbits survived.
"The planetary system did not completely disappear. Some surviving rocky bodies may have been gravitationally perturbed onto highly eccentric orbits that brought them close to the white dwarf," Lagos-Vilches said.
"Objects that came sufficiently close were disrupted by the white dwarf's gravitational force. Their material was spread into a debris disc containing dust and gas. However, two relatively large rocky bodies may have survived within this debris," Lagos-Vilches said. 
The presence of the two bodies may help explain the distribution of the surrounding material into a pair of concentric gaseous rings, Lagos-Vilches said. 
"The outer ring is strongly depleted in magnesium compared with the inner ring. This suggests that they may originate from different parent bodies, or possibly from different layers of a rocky body that was disrupted when it went too close to the white dwarf due to its strong gravitational field," Lagos-Vilches said.
A GLIMPSE OF THE FUTURE
In about 5 billion years, the sun will become a red giant, Lagos-Vilches said.
"It will eventually lose its outer layers and become a white dwarf. The inner solar system will be dramatically affected. Mercury and Venus are expected to be engulfed by the expanding sun, while there is still no clear consensus on whether Earth will also be engulfed during this phase. The fate of the outer planets is different. Jupiter, Saturn and the more distant bodies should have a much better chance of surviving," Lagos-Vilches said.
After the sun becomes a white dwarf, surviving planetary remnants, moons and asteroids could potentially be drawn close enough to the white dwarf to be torn apart by gravitational forces.
"A debris disc like the one around J1328−1450 could therefore represent one possible stage in the very distant future of our own planetary system," Lagos-Vilches said.

Source: Reuters

Russia pounds power facilities around Kyiv, damages major bridge

By Dan Peleschuk
KYIV, Nov 7 (Reuters) – Russian forces hammered energy infrastructure around Ukraine’s capital with missiles and drones overnight, straining Kyiv’s power supply and heating systems as temperatures headed towards zero, officials said on Saturday.

Explosions rocked the city as Russia fired multiple waves of ballistic missiles, several of which hit and damaged the Northern Bridge across the Dnipro River, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko.

Strikes on energy facilities outside Kyiv — including systems sending power from two nuclear plants to the city and Ukraine’s central regions — caused serious damage, the energy ministry said.

Show Full Article

“The capital is facing serious difficulties with its electricity, water, and heat supplies,” President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on X, adding that substations in five other regions were also hit.

He said Russia had launched 36 ballistic missiles, only four of which were intercepted, according to Ukraine’s air force. It added that air defences had downed 149 out of 172 drones.

AT LEAST TWO PEOPLE REPORTED KILLED

At least two people were killed and around a dozen others wounded across Ukraine in the overnight attacks, which also damaged homes, businesses and non-residential buildings, authorities said.

Moscow’s defence ministry said it carried out a massive strike on what it described as targets in Ukraine’s military-industrial sector, as well as energy and transport infrastructure in and around Kyiv.

Russia has stepped up air attacks on Ukraine as its ground offensive has largely stalled, pounding energy infrastructure in major cities with difficult-to-intercept missiles and drones more than 4-1/2 years into its full-scale invasion.

It has expanded its campaign in recent weeks to target Kyiv’s bridges, snarling traffic in the city of more than 3 million people.

Saturday’s strikes come days before a new round of three-way talks in Abu Dhabi between Ukrainian and Russian officials, as part of a US-backed peace push that has so far yielded few results.

“Russia is preparing for trilateral talks by launching ballistic missiles at Ukraine’s critical infrastructure,” Zelenskiy said on X.

The attacks also follow recent US midterm elections that have raised hopes in Ukraine for stronger support against Russia’s war from a Democratic-controlled Congress.

“We are counting on the US Congress to give more attention to Ukraine, because Russia keeps increasing the number of its attacks,” Zelenskiy added.

(Editing by Andrew Heavens)

Nov 7 (Reuters) – Iran executed a Baluch man for involvement in an armed attack on a police station in the southeast of the country in which several officers were killed or wounded, Iranian media reported on Saturday.

Mohammad Aref Shahbakhsh, identified by the semi-official media as a member of the Sunni militant group Jaish al-Adl, was convicted of armed rebellion and “waging war against God” in connection with the attack on the Qaleh Bid police station in Khash, in Sistan-Baluchestan province.

The report did not specify when the attack took place or how many police officers were killed or wounded.

Show Full Article

Jaish al-Adl, which operates in southeastern Iran near the border with Pakistan, has carried out numerous attacks against Iranian security forces.

Russian strikes hit power facilities around Kyiv, damage major bridge

KYIV, Nov 7 (Reuters) – Russian forces launched missile and drone attacks on Ukraine’s capital Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight, damaging energy infrastructure and a major bridge across the Dnipro River, officials said on Saturday.

Explosions rocked the city as Russia fired multiple waves of ballistic missiles, several of them hitting the Northern Bridge, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko.

He described an “extremely difficult” situation for power, heating and water supplies in Kyiv, where temperatures hovered near freezing on Saturday morning. Governor Tymur Tkachenko said energy facilities in at least three districts of the Kyiv region had been hit.

Show Full Article

One person was killed and eight people including a child were wounded in the overnight attack, which also damaged homes and non-residential buildings, authorities said.

Moscow’s defence ministry said it carried out a massive strike on what it described as targets in Ukraine’s military-industrial sector, as well as energy and transport infrastructure in and around Kyiv.

Russia has stepped up air attacks on Ukraine as its ground offensive has largely stalled, pounding energy infrastructure in major cities with difficult-to-intercept missiles and drones more than 4-1/2 years into its full-scale invasion.

It has expanded its campaign in recent weeks to target Kyiv’s bridges, snarling traffic in the city of more than 3 million.

Saturday’s strikes also damaged energy infrastructure in the central Zhytomyr region, the regional governor and Russia’s defence ministry said.

They come days before a new round of three-way talks in Abu Dhabi between Ukrainian and Russian officials, as part of a US-backed peace push that has so far yielded few results.

(Editing by Andrew Heavens)

Nov 7 : Brazilian club Santos FC said on Friday it had appointed Neymar's father and agent, Neymar Sr., as its CEO.
Neymar's father has played a key role in his son's career and founded the agency NR Sports, which holds the rights to the Santos player's name and image.
According to reports in Brazilian media, Neymar Sr.'s contract runs until December and he will stay on in the role if Santos president Marcelo Teixeira is re-elected next month.
Santos are ninth in the Brazilian Serie A standings with 47 points from 34 matches.

"We have been working daily to find solutions and alternatives to improve Santos's situation and strengthen our management," Teixeira said in a statement.
"The arrival of Neymar Sr. as the new CEO represents one more step in this process. I am confident that, with his experience and knowledge, we will be able to move forward even further and, together, build an ever-stronger club."
Former Barcelona and Paris St Germain player Neymar, Brazil's all-time leading scorer with 80 goals in 130 appearances, returned to his childhood club Santos in 2025.
He was part of the Brazil squad at this year's World Cup in North America, but in late July said he no longer wanted to play for the national team, weeks after suggesting his international career had ended following their last-16 defeat by Norway.

items.title: Finland considers Ukraine-style anti-tank barriers as Russia rearms
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: The country is assessing how defensive structures used in Ukraine would withstand harsh northern weather as Russia rebuilds its military capacity, Finnish Army chief Pasi Välimäki said ...
items.body: By Kirsi Heikel Finland is studying Ukraine-style anti-tank obstacles to bolster its border with Russia as it works to strengthen defenses on Nato’s eastern flank against a rapidly rearming foe.   Lieutenant General Pasi Välimäki, commander of the Finnish Army, said in an interview that Russia had already begun rebuilding its military capacity, even as its full-scale invasion of Ukraine grinds into a fifth year. In that conflict, Kyiv’s forces have used extensive defensive lines and anti-tank obstacles to slow attackers. Neither side has found a reliable way to break through them and restore large-scale movement and maneuver, Välimäki said. Sharing a 1,340-kilometer (830-mile) border with Russia, accounting for about half of Nato’s land frontier with that country, Finland must determine how structures similar to those used in Ukraine would fare in harsh northern weather. “Conditions in Finland are more challenging,” Välimäki said. “If we build fortifications and dig anti-tank ditches or obstacles as deep as those in Ukraine, how long does it take before our environment turns them into artificial ponds?” Russia’s efforts to replenish its weapons stockpiles are starting to show some effects, he said, with T-90 tanks, BMP-3 infantry fighting vehicles and 2S19 self-propelled howitzers being delivered to storage sites. Finland lacks the capacity to prevent that rearming. Rather, the goal is to deter Russia by convincing its military that an attack would fail, he said. “Everything we are doing now is about creating a threshold so that Russia does not go any further, whether we are talking about the alliance or Finland,” Välimäki said. Finland continued conscription and maintained territorial defense reserves after the Cold War, even as many European nations reduced their forces. Despite a population of just 5.6 million, its military can call on about 280,000 troops in wartime. “When the war in Ukraine began, we improved our readiness and put 60,000 people through refresher training over two years,” Välimäki said. “We also quickly began replenishing stocks of critical materiel.” Finland is now carrying out an overhaul of its land forces that will run through the end of the 2030s, covering equipment, force structure, readiness and the capacity to sustain combat. The basic approach — deterring an attack by being prepared — hasn’t changed, Välimäki said. What has changed is the scale required.  “The scale of the ammunition, production systems and trained personnel that we need to have ready for use is different from what it was before 2022,” he said. “It has to be larger, more sustainable and technologically more advanced than before.” Finland will spend at least as much on the overhaul of its land forces as on its ongoing strategic Navy and Air Force programs combined, the Defense Ministry said in a written statement. Those programs have total funding of €11.6 billion ($13 billion). As part of a much broader procurement drive, Finland is expanding its Hanwha Aerospace Co. Ltd. K9 self-propelled howitzer fleet, modernising its heavy multiple-launch rocket systems to fire almost 500 kilometers, and preparing to replace its BMP-2 infantry fighting vehicles. Attacks on Ukraine have shown the scale of the air and missile threat Finland may face. Under the alliance’s Eastern Flank Deterrence Line concept, it isn’t enough to shoot down incoming missiles and drones — defenders must also be able to strike the launchers before they fire, Välimäki said.  “For Finns, this is a difficult issue, because it means hitting targets on the Russian side,” he said.  Finland has already begun replacing its F/A-18 Hornets with 64 Lockheed Martin Corp. F-35A fighters, with the first aircraft delivered. It has also ordered Israel’s David’s Sling missile-defense system, produced by Rafael Advanced Defense Systems Ltd., which has seen extensive action in the Iran war. Välimäki rejects the idea that new technology has made traditional weapons obsolete. Drones have become a major part of the battlefield, Välimäki said, adding that they are only one element to consider. Ukraine has also underscored the need to replenish equipment and ammunition during a prolonged conflict, and Välimäki wants domestic production that can expand rapidly.  “What I would like Finland to have is the ability to scale for mass-production in large volumes — production for readiness and daily training consumption that can be maintained in peacetime and scaled up tenfold in crisis and conflict,” he said. The push reflects a fundamental constraint on how Finland can fight a much larger opponent on the eastern flank of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation. “We do not want a war of attrition,” Välimäki said. “We are a country of five million people, and we cannot operate on that logic.”

items.title: カタール、米イラン仲介継続　「大きな進展」と首相
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［７日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［７日　ロイター］ - カタールのムハンマド首相は、地域情勢が制御不能に陥るのを防ぐため、米国とイランの仲介を続けていると述べた。衛星テレビ局アルジャジーラが７日報じた。

ムハンマド氏は、米政権は中間選挙後も解決策を見いだす意欲を維持しており、合意を目指す姿勢に変わりがないことを示していると述べた。

また、これまでに大きな進展があったとし、解決に向けた合意に達することができるとの自信を示した。「完璧な合意に達するまで待つわけにはいかない。良い合意に達することを望んでいる」と語った。

一方、イランの準国営タスニム通信は７日、初期段階の情報によるとケシム島にミサイル２発が着弾したもようだと報じた。被害の有無について公式情報はないとしている。米国は現時点で攻撃について発表していない。

トランプ米大統領は３日の中間選挙に先立つ数週間、イランへの攻撃を見合わせていたが、域内諸国は米国が選挙後に攻撃を再開する可能性があると見込んでいた。イランは、新たな攻撃を受ければ近隣諸国にある米国とイスラエルの標的を攻撃して報復すると繰り返し表明している。

items.title: 英メーガン妃の父親逮捕、子どもの性的虐待画像所持の疑い
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ワシントン　６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ワシントン　６日　ロイター］ - 英国のヘンリー王子の妻メーガン妃の父親トーマス・マークル容疑者（８２）が６日、子どもの性的虐待画像を所持した疑いで逮捕、訴追された。画像はカリフォルニア州の貸倉庫から見つかり、裸の未成年の少女と容疑者が一緒に写った写真も含まれている。

パテル米連邦捜査局（ＦＢＩ）長官によると、容疑者はフロリダ州で連邦捜査官に身柄を拘束された。英紙デーリー・メールによると、容疑者は同州の介護施設に入所しており、車椅子を使用しているという。

パテル氏は声明で「罪のない子どもたちを標的にし、犯罪行為によってその純真さを奪おうとした疑いがある」と説明した。司法省によると、有罪となれば最高で禁錮２０年の刑が科される可能性がある。 

容疑者は、フロリダ州タンパで連邦治安判事の前に初出廷した。ロサンゼルスの連邦検察当局の声明によると、判事は自宅拘禁と電子監視に従うことを条件に、裁判を待つ間の釈放を命じた。 

声明によると、罪状認否はまだ行われておらず、数週間先になる見通し。

英王室とメーガン妃の広報担当者は、コメントの要請に応じなかった。

items.title: India in Final-Stage Talks to Expand Missile Sale to Philippines, Sources Say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: India is in final-stage talks to expand its sale of supersonic cruise missiles to the Philippines, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters, as New Delhi nears completion of deliveries under a 2022 deal. The Philippines is expected to buy about five …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
India is in final-stage talks to expand its sale of supersonic cruise missiles to the Philippines, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters, as New Delhi nears completion of deliveries under a 2022 deal.

The Philippines is expected to buy about five BrahMos systems, nearly 60 missiles in total, in a deal potentially worth $700 million to $800 million, two of the Indian sources said.

“Manila has shown interest again to procure about 5 systems of the BrahMos, and they now view India as a very reliable partner,” one Indian source said.

New Delhi’s latest likely deal with the Philippines, which is modernizing its military and strengthening coastal defenses as tensions rise in the disputed South China Sea, is much higher than the last $375 million order of BrahMos for naval use.

BrahMos, developed jointly by India and Russia, is among the world’s fastest cruise missiles and can be launched from land, sea and air platforms.

Arsenio Andolong, Philippines defense ministry spokesperson, told Reuters that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. had expressed his desire to acquire additional BrahMos missiles. Andolong did not offer more details.

Speaking virtually at the Delhi Defense Dialogue on Wednesday, Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said the Philippines hoped to secure more BrahMos units and had shared a wish list with Indian authorities to tailor the system to the Philippine environment.

Reuters is the first to report the size and value of the deal.

The additional purchase comes at a time when Manila is building its military strength as tension escalates with Beijing over overlapping claims in the South China Sea, where the two countries have clashed in recent years.

India’s defence and foreign ministries, as well as missile maker BrahMos Aerospace, did not respond to requests for comment.

Interest in the BrahMos system has increased since last year’s four-day conflict between India and Pakistan, when India used the weapons system for the first time in battle.

In July, Delhi announced the supply of BrahMos missiles to Indonesia and has also signed a deal with Vietnam. It is in talks on the system with a number of other countries including UAE , Thailand, South Africa and Brazil.

India’s defense exports for the fiscal year to March reached 384.24 billion rupees ($4.11 billion), a jump of more than 62% from the same period the year before, government data showed.

FAST

WASHINGTON, Nov 7 : Environmental groups worldwide are using artificial intelligence to analyze climate data, track forest fires and count endangered wildlife – embracing a technology they also warn is driving a surge in electricity demand, water use and greenhouse-gas emissions.
The contradiction is forcing these organizations to justify their AI use in carrying out missions to combat climate change or protect natural resources.
"We recognize that AI can come with environmental costs, and we need to be thoughtful about how we use it," said Ali Swanson, AI lead at the US nonprofit Conservation International. "But at a time when the climate and biodiversity crises are becoming more urgent, AI can help us move faster and make better use of the information we're collecting."
The group recently started using AI to assess hotspots detected by satellites and send real-time alerts to community forest patrols about potential wildfires in remote and environmentally sensitive parts of Cambodia.

Reuters interviewed 15 major environmental, conservation and development organizations about their AI use. All said they used the technology in some form and expressed concern about the environmental impact of the data centers powering it. The centers, filled with servers, can require vast amounts of electricity, along with water for cooling.
It's a global dilemma for individuals, governments and industries balancing AI's benefits with its enormous risks. The tradeoffs likely will grab attention at the UN's COP31 climate conference this month, when host Turkey will call on governments, businesses and other institutions to sign a pledge outlining principles to ensure AI is developed and deployed sustainably.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres wants major AI companies to publicly disclose their systems' environmental impacts.
Researchers at the United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health estimate the global data-center footprint could more than double by 2030, reaching a size about twice that of Jakarta, the Indonesian megalopolis.
The International Energy Agency, meanwhile, estimates global data centers will consume about 945 terawatt-hours of electricity annually by 2030, producing the equivalent of more than 300 million metric tons of carbon dioxide. That's double current consumption and about equal to Japan's annual electricity use.
The agency also projects that global data center water consumption will increase from about 560 billion liters (147.9 billion gallons) in 2023 to about 1.2 trillion liters (317 billion gallons) annually by 2030.
Technology giants including Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet's Google have reported rising emissions linked in part to data center expansion, raising questions about their ability to meet their own long-term climate goals.
Amazon told Reuters its artificial-intelligence products were among the most sustainable due to the company's purchases of low-carbon energy and its efforts to use power and water efficiently.
Microsoft and Google didn't respond to requests for comment.
BREAKTHROUGHS ONCE THOUGHT IMPOSSIBLE
Many of the organizations that spoke to Reuters believe AI's benefits currently outweigh its costs because the technology is enabling work that was previously difficult, expensive or impossible.
Kenya's Save the Elephants, a partner of the Wildlife Conservation Network, said it is using machine learning to improve population surveys and study elephant communication.
Frank Pope, the group's chief executive, said an aerial survey of Kenya's largest protected area last year generated roughly 200,000 images that took nine people nine months to review manually. AI models trained on Nvidia's GeForce graphics platforms can now complete similar analyses in hours.
"The results have been eye-opening," Pope said. "We found that human surveys were missing about a third of the elephants, roughly half of zebras and giraffes, and three-quarters of oryx populations."
More accurate wildlife data can help secure financing for conservation, he said.
"Ultimately, these tools make nature measurable and therefore investable," he said. "That's a critical transformation, if we're going to conserve biodiversity at scale."
At the institute founded by the late conservation icon Jane Goodall, researchers are using AI to digitize decades of field notes about chimpanzee behavior in Tanzania's Gombe National Park.
The project was once expected to take 13-15 years because the records were written by hand using the local Kiha language and scientific shorthand.
Thanks to a tool developed with Amazon Web Services, the notes can now be scanned, translated and structured in minutes, slashing the time needed to about two years, said Lilian Pintea, the Jane Goodall Institute's vice president of conservation science.
During her lifetime, Pintea said, Goodall supported the use of AI to advance conservation science, provided people remained firmly in control of how it was used.
"AI technology should be seen as tools which are human-centered," Pintea said.
LIMITING THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT
Some organizations are experimenting with ways to limit the environmental impact of their AI use.
The World Resources Institute (WRI), a research group that uses AI to accelerate its climate and environmental analyses, said it limits resource-intensive applications such as generating videos and images, while caching AI query results so identical searches don't need to be reprocessed.
The US-based Nature Conservancy has adopted a similar approach. It uses AI to analyze video captured on commercial fishing vessels for information on how many fish of different species they catch. But instead of uploading huge numbers of videos to centralized data centers, it has installed AI-powered digital cameras to process information aboard the vessels, reducing energy use and data-transfer requirements, said Vienna Saccomanno, a senior scientist at the organization.
"It takes a lot of engineering to make computation on the edge possible," she said. "This was worth it to reduce both our carbon footprint and deliver these sustainability insights."
Greenpeace International said it, too, uses some AI tools, mainly because software platforms it relies upon include AI features.
It's imposing internal guidelines emphasizing transparency, human oversight and "intentional" AI use, the group said. But it would prefer to sidestep the technology due to its environmental impacts and is pushing back hard on the data center buildout.
"While other organizations are asking how to use AI responsibly, Greenpeace is asking whether it's necessary to build all these massive data centers in the first place," said Katrin Xueying Wu, a climate and energy campaigner with the organization.
Other groups now see AI as vital to effective environmental activism.
"It's our job to save the planet. If we can do that more effectively and efficiently with the limited resources we've got by using AI, then we have to seriously engage in that possibility," said Stuart Butchart, chief scientist at UK-based BirdLife International.
"If we don't do it, then we're sort of being derelict in our duty."

(Additonal reporting by Simon Jessop in London and Kate Abnett in Brussels; Editing by Richard Valdmanis and Alexandra Zavis)

Source: Reuters

FAST

Nov 7 : India fast bowler Mohammed Shami said he would continue playing white-ball cricket and remain available for domestic multi-day matches after retiring from test cricket on Friday, bringing the curtain down on a 13-year red-ball career.
The 36-year-old, who took 229 wickets in 64 tests after making a memorable debut against West Indies in 2013, announced his decision in a video posted on social media on the anniversary of his first test appearance.
"Let's end this 13-year journey here today," Shami said.
"I made my debut today, and today I am taking retirement. I am leaving this, but I will continue to play white-ball cricket, whether it is IPL or domestic.

"If it is needed for fitness, I will continue to play days cricket. So, this was the journey so far. I started it today, and I am ending it today."
His final test appearance came in the World Test Championship final against Australia in 2023, but he continued to play limited-overs cricket before injuries and fitness concerns hampered his appearances for India.
Shami, India's all-time leading wicket-taker in 50-over World Cups with 55 wickets, last featured for India in a one-day international against New Zealand last year and in a Twenty20 match against England in February 2025.
He currently represents Bengal in domestic cricket and plays for Lucknow Super Giants in the Indian Premier League.

“トランプ氏大敗”で世界同時株安 日経平均は過去3番目の下げ幅 余波は政権にも…閣僚に「辞任検討」「弾劾案」報道【news23】

TBSテレビ

2026年11月7日(土) 14:16

国際
news23

歴史的大敗で“トランプ離れ”か　閣僚に「辞任検討」「弾劾案」報道

ただ、トランプ氏にとっては、世界的な株安もどこ吹く風。

トランプ大統領

「これほど多くの事を成し遂げた大統領は他にいない。この執務室は勝利の象徴で、威厳のある場所だ」

こう話し署名したのは、“勝利の象徴”の「大統領執務室」を国定記念物に指定する文書です。

前任のバイデン氏政権の2023年ごろはシンプルだった執務室が、この2年で金の装飾が施され、トランプ氏好みの空間へと変貌を遂げました。

トランプ大統領

「誰にも触れさせない。愚か者が壊したり解体することは認めない」

2年の任期を残しながら、退任後のレガシー作りに躍起になるトランプ大統領ですが、その足元で政権の中枢は揺らぎ始めています。

ブルームバーグ通信

「ルビオ国務長官が政権からの離脱を検討している」

“次期大統領選の有力候補”とされるルビオ国務長官の“辞任検討”の報道。

本人は否定したとの報道もありますが、選挙結果を受け、政権との距離を置き始めたとの見方が広がりました。

さらにブルームバーグ通信は、9日の週にも与党・共和党の下院議員がヘグセス国防長官に対する弾劾訴追決議案を提出する見通しだと報道。

大敗の余波が広がる中、トランプ政権内の混乱は続きそうです。

items.title: “Do Gaz Zamin”: India’s last Mughal emperor died today 164 years ago; but his life of pain and tragedy lives
items.summary: The man who was the last scion of India and South Asia’s most powerful ruling house, Bahadur Shah Zafar, died today 164 years ago in Rangoon (Yangon today), British-ruled Burma.
items.body:
“Do Gaz Zamin”: India’s last Mughal emperor died today 164 years ago; but his life of pain and tragedy lives The man who was the last scion of India and South Asia’s most powerful ruling house, Bahadur Shah Zafar, died today 164 years ago in Rangoon (Yangon today), British-ruled Burma.
ANI | Updated: 07-11-2026 18:29 IST | Created: 07-11-2026 18:29 IST

the Red Fort, a magnificent 17th-century red sandstone structure in Delhi where mutinous Indian soldiers proclaimed the ageing and frail Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar as ruler of India in May 1857. (Photo/REUTERS). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

India

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The man who was the last scion of India and South Asia’s most powerful ruling house, Bahadur Shah Zafar, died today 164 years ago in Rangoon (Yangon today), British-ruled Burma. Zafar, the last emperor of the Mughal dynasty that ruled the subcontinent from 1526 to 1858, has become the symbol of the fickleness of power in popular imagination. Born to one of the strongest empires in human history, Zafar died alone and most importantly, far removed from the environs that he had called home throughout his life.
Bahadur Shah was born on October 24, 1775, in Shahjahanabad, the Mughal citadel of Delhi that his illustrious ancestor, Shah Jahan, had built. His parents were Emperor Akbar Shah II and Lal Bai. Most know ‘Zafar’ as a poet, for the name was his takhallus. But to historians, Bahadur Shah’s life is also important while studying the Great Revolt of 1857, also known by other terms such as ‘The Sepoy Mutiny’ or ‘The First War of Indian Independence’, depending on which side of the fence one is on.
The British East India Company had received permission to trade in the subcontinent from Zafar’s ancestor, Jehangir. Slowly, it developed into the strongest political force in the region until it became the de facto ruler. However, the Company Bahadur’s policies led to deep resentment. Things came to a head in 1857 when rumours of the cartridges of a brand new rifle for the Company’s Sepoys being laced with cow and pig fat began doing the rounds.
On May 9, 1857, the soldiers in Meerut Cantonment revolted and rode towards Delhi. Crossing the Yamuna over a bridge of boats, they entered the city on May 11, where they declared the frail Zafar as the Shahenshah-e-Hind (Emperor of India/Emperor of Hindustan). Aged 82 and initially reluctant, Zafar lent his name, seal, and formal audience to the uprising, becoming its nominal head.
After the British retook Delhi following a string of bloody battles in 1857, Major William Hodson captured Zafar and other members of the royal family on September 21, 1857, at Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, where they had sought refuge. A day later, Hodson shot and killed Zafar's sons, Mirza Mughal and Mirza Khizr Sultan, and grandson Mirza Abu Bakr in cold blood. The spot is now known ‘Khooni Darwaza’ and lies near Maulana Azad Medical College.
As for Zafar, he was put on trial at the Red Fort and later exiled to Rangoon (Yangon, where he died in 1862 on November 7. It is in Rangoon that Zafar penned an immortal verse that has perhaps enshrined his memory among millions in the region:
Kitna hai bad-naseeb 'Zafar' dafn ke liye, Do gaz zamin bhi na mili ku-e-yar mein.
(English): How unfortunate is 'Zafar' for burial,
Not even two yards of land were found in the beloved alley (referring to his homeland, Delhi). His life shows that even the most powerful dynasties cannot stand the march of Time and that only change is here to stay. Perhaps that is what makes the story of his life touching and appealing at the same time. (ANI)

items.title: ＮＢＡ＝セルティックス快勝、シクサーズは連勝ストップ　ＮＢＡカップ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［６日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）は６日、シーズン中のトーナメント戦であるＮＢＡカップを各地で行い、東カンファレンスＣ組のセルティックスはホーネッツに１１９─８０で快勝した。

セルティックスはジェイソン・テイタムが両チーム最多の３４得点に、８リバウンド、９アシストとトリプルダブル級の活躍。チームは前半だけで７０得点を挙げてホーネッツを突き放した。同組のホークスはウィザーズに１３９─１３２で勝利した。

Ｂ組のキャバリアーズはセブンティシクサーズを１１９─９５で下した。ドノバン・ミッチェルが２３得点、７リバウンド、８アシストで攻撃をけん引。シクサーズは公式戦連勝が５でストップした。Ａ組ではラプターズがバックスに１２１─１０７で勝利した。

西カンファレンスＢ組のサンダーは、グリズリーズに１２８─９７で快勝した。エイジェイ・ミッチェルが両チーム最多の３５得点をマーク。シェイ・ギルジャス・アレクサンダーは２８得点を挙げた。

同組のティンバーウルブズはペリカンズに１１５─１０９で競り勝った。Ａ組ではマーベリックスがジャズに１１２─１００で勝利した。

items.title: SpaceX director Donald Harrison resigns from board a day after US election
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: Harrison, who joined SpaceX's board in 2015 as part of Google's investment, stepped down on November 4. The exit comes as independent directors of SpaceX and Tesla consider a potential merger ...
items.body: By Carmen Arroyo SpaceX board member Donald Harrison resigned from the role after more than a decade, leaving the company as a group of independent directors consider a potential merger with Tesla Inc. Harrison informed SpaceX of his intention to resign on Nov. 4, one day after the US midterm election, according to a SpaceX filing issued after the close Friday. The company said his decision was not due to any disagreement with the company. Harrison joined the board in 2015 as part of Google’s investment in Musk’s rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company. He was an independent director and still works for Google parent Alphabet Inc., leading its corporate partnerships and development team. SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees of independent directors to consider a potential combination, Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk said last month. There’s a push to announce a deal by the first half of next year so that it closes during this administration, Bloomberg News reported. Musk hasn’t said which board members are on the companies’ special committees. Harrison was among the directors SpaceX considers independent, alongside Ira Ehrenpreis, Roelof Botha, Luke Nosek, Steve Jurvetson and Randy Glein. Alphabet remains one of SpaceX’s leading backers, with the second-biggest shareholding after Musk. The investment weighed on the earnings results Alphabet reported last week due to SpaceX shares declining last quarter. Google and SpaceX have rival AI models and chatbots in Gemini and Grok that compete with Anthropic PBC’s Claude and OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

Nov 7 : Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to being left out of England's squad by helping his club Everton to a 3-1 comeback victory over Coventry City in the Premier League on Friday.
Dewsbury-Hall was not named in the squad for this month's Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain, with England boss Thomas Tuchel saying that the Everton midfielder had been close to making the cut.
A few hours after the squad was announced, Dewsbury-Hall scored to round off Everton's win and add to teammate Thierno Barry's two goals.
"It was a disappointing morning, I'm not going to lie. It's a massive dream of mine to play for my country. I know I was close," the 28-year-old told Sky Sports after the home win.

"I've got the mentality. I'll keep pushing and pushing and see what happens."
England, second in Nations League Group C, host Croatia at Wembley on November 12 before travelling to Madrid to face Spain three days later.

Ahead of Trump-Xi meetings, US presses China on trade pledges

"I emphasized the importance of China fully and immediately honouring its commitments, raised concerns about recent Chinese actions and underscored that progress depends on concrete results," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a social media post.

FAST

WASHINGTON: The Trump administration warned a top Chinese official on Friday (Nov 6) that Beijing must immediately implement its commitments under a nearly year-old trade agreement, particularly on delivery of rare earths and other critical minerals and agricultural purchases, the United States Trade Representative's Office said.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer urged Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in a call to implement terms of the pact agreed in Busan, South Korea, in October 2025, the US agencies said.
"During the call, Ambassador Greer emphasized the critical importance of China taking concrete actions to fully implement its past commitments, particularly as they relate to agricultural purchases, rare earths and other critical minerals," USTR said in a statement.
During the call, China expressed "serious concern" over recent US trade restrictions targeting Beijing, China's official Xinhua news agency said.

But He, China's lead negotiator on trade relations with the US, agreed with his US counterparts to continue using consultation for "stable and positive" development of trade ties, Xinhua reported.
Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are expected to meet at the summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China, on Nov 18 and 19, and the Group of 20 summit in Miami on Dec 14 and 15.
Greer said the Trump administration will pursue balanced trade with China by "monitoring compliance of past commitments while unlocking lasting benefits for American farmers, ranchers, manufacturers, and workers".
Greer, Bessent and other US officials have frequently complained about difficulties that US companies say they are experiencing in receiving sufficient quantities of rare earths and other critical minerals from China under the Busan agreement. The US says the deal was designed to lift restrictions put in place in 2025 during a period of tariff escalations between the world's two largest economies.
The Busan trade deal, which expires on Jan 10, capped US tariffs on Chinese goods implemented during Trump's second term at about 20 per cent. China has pledged to buy 25 million metric tons of US soybeans for the next three years and boost purchases of other American farm goods by US$17 billion.
"I emphasized the importance of China fully and immediately honouring its commitments, raised concerns about recent Chinese actions and underscored that progress depends on concrete results," Bessent said in a social media post.
The US will "closely assess China’s implementation of the arrangement", the Treasury said in a statement.
Beijing has signaled tariff concessions remain central to its aims, with its commerce ministry saying on Thursday that China was open to buying more US farm goods, but only if the two sides implement their reciprocal tariff-cut agreement.
Following a September summit between Xi and Trump in Washington, the two sides proposed a US$60 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts, including roughly US$17 billion worth of US farm goods that China imported in 2024, though the plan has not been finalised.
The White House said in May that Beijing had agreed to buy US$17 billion of US agricultural goods annually from 2026, with this year's target adjusted on a prorated basis. Those purchases were in addition to a commitment made in October last year to buy US soybeans.

Source: Reuters/cf

Nov 6 : SpaceX disclosed on Friday that Google executive Donald Harrison has resigned from the rockets-to-AI company's board after more than a decade.

• Harrison notified SpaceX of his resignation on November 4, and it took effect immediately

items.title: ケニアのカルト教団指導者に禁錮200年、子ども190人に餓死強要
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
(文中の余分な記号を削除しました)

［モンバサ（ケニア）　６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
(文中の余分な記号を削除しました)

［モンバサ（ケニア）　６日　ロイター］ - ケニアの裁判所は６日、子ども１９０人を餓死させ森に埋めたとして、カルト教団指導者ポール・マッケンジー被告に禁錮２００年の判決を言い渡した。事件全体の犠牲者は５００人に上ると見られており、現代のカルト教団による大量殺人として最悪級の規模となった。

禁錮２００年の内訳は、餓死による殺人に１００年、直接的な殺害に１００年。

検察によると、マッケンジー被告はケニア東部インド洋沿岸近くの森林で、終末論を唱えるキリスト教系教団を率いていた。世界の終わりが来る前に天国に到達するため、子どもとともに餓死するよう信者に命じていた。

被告の共犯者は、命令に従うよう信者を脅したり、暴行を加えたりしていた。やせ細った遺体が各所の浅い墓から見つかったほか、便所に捨てられた遺体もあった。生き埋めにされた子どももいたという。

今回の裁判の対象となったのは子ども１９０人と成人１人の犠牲者だが、ケニア国家人権委員会によると、森林では最終的に４４８人の遺体が見つかった。マッケンジー被告は、３０キロ離れた村の別の場所で見つかった５２人の殺害を命じた罪にも問われており、これを合わせると犠牲者は計５００人に上る可能性がある。

Paraguay president ousted and placed under house arrest, successor sworn in

Santiago Peña was ousted from the presidency about an hour beforehand in a unanimous Senate vote, with lawmakers citing questions over his past links to the collapsed digital bank ueno that had provided accounts for nearly half of Paraguay's population.

Paraguay's President Santiago Pena speaks during an interview with Reuters, in Asuncion, Paraguay Aug 21, 2024. (Photo: Reuters/Cesar Olmedo)

ASUNCION, Paraguay: Pedro Alliana was sworn in as Paraguay's new president on Friday (Nov 6) just as authorities put his impeached predecessor Santiago Peña under house arrest, the latest developments in a fast-moving political and financial crisis triggered by the collapse of a digital bank.
Prosecutors speaking outside Peña's house in Asunción said charges were still being determined but could include influence peddling. Peña was ordered to appear at the prosecutor's office on Saturday morning.

Paraguay's Vice President Pedro Alliana is sworn in after President Santiago Pena was removed from office in an impeachment trial, in Asuncion, Paraguay, Nov 6, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Cesar Olmedo)

Peña was ousted from the presidency about an hour beforehand in a unanimous Senate vote, with lawmakers citing questions over his past links to the collapsed digital bank ueno that had provided accounts for nearly half of Paraguay's population.
Although Peña offered his resignation on Thursday, the Senate chose to finalise the impeachment process rather than accept, and swiftly moved to install his second-in-command, Alliana.

By the time of his arrest, dozens of protesters had gathered outside Peña's residence. Police installed a security cordon around the property.
The turmoil began earlier this week when Paraguay's central bank intervened in ueno, whose customers include many people who had not previously had access to a bank account.
The bank had grown rapidly since launching in 2021. But questions had emerged over ueno's lending practices and its ties to Paraguay's political and financial elite - including Peña, who until last year was a shareholder in ueno's holding company, and the central bank chief Carlos Carvallo, who had headed ueno until 2023.
Prosecutors on Friday also issued an arrest warrant for Carvallo, who resigned earlier this week as authorities launched last-ditch proceedings to prevent the lender dissolving. Eight former ueno executives have already been detained.
Others from Peña's inner circle also resigned, including his interior minister, chief of staff and two advisers.
The impeachment charges that led to his removal alleged that Peña had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank.
Peña denied any wrongdoing and said the affair was a regulatory issue. The central bank has denied any conflict of interest, saying Carvallo recused himself from all decisions related to ueno.
FROZEN ACCESS TO FUNDS The political crisis has spilled onto the streets, with demonstrators flocking to downtown Asuncion demanding accountability for ueno's collapse and faster compensation for depositors whose savings remain frozen.
Small groups of protesters gathered opposite the headquarters of the central bank on Friday, chanting "We want our money."

People protest outside Congress during a session to discuss President Santiago Pena's resignation, days after Paraguay's central bank took over Ueno Bank amid a solvency crisis, in Asuncion, Paraguay, Thursday, Nov 5, 2026. (Photo: AP/Jorge Saenz)

Those who have been unable to access their accounts include pensioners who receive state benefits through ueno. Peña earlier this week approved legislation to help accelerate payments to affected depositors and some account holders began recovering their money on Thursday.
Prospects for a lengthy political transition have drawn attention from investors, especially in neighboring Brazil, Paraguay's largest economic partner. Regulators have sought to reassure markets by guaranteeing most deposits and containing risks to the wider financial system.
A Brazilian government source told Reuters that Brazil's immediate concern was avoiding social instability in Paraguay and ensuring the banking crisis is resolved without triggering wider unrest.
"Protests over frozen savings will intensify if Peña's exit appears to grant him impunity or if payouts to depositors and pensioners stall," said Mariano Machado, Americas principal analyst at Verisk Maplecroft.

Source: Reuters/cf

FAST

SYDNEY, Nov 7 : Former Australian cricketer Usman Khawaja said in a new autobiography excerpted on Saturday that discussions about ball-tampering during Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa were more widespread within the team than Cricket Australia's investigation found.
The "Sandpapergate" scandal over Australia's scuffing of the ball with sandpaper in the March 2018 test in Cape Town sparked a major integrity crisis for Cricket Australia.
In a statement on Saturday, the governing body defended its 2018 probe that concluded prior knowledge was confined to three players — Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft.
Khawaja, in extracts of his autobiography published in the Sydney Morning Herald on Saturday, claimed "open, lighthearted discussions" were held during the South Africa series about ways to scuff up the ball, including by using sandpaper.

He said discussion of tampering was not confined to batters, bowlers or staff but extended throughout the team.
"It was all of us," Khawaja, a former top-order batsman who played 88 tests for Australia, said in the book, according to the newspaper.
Khawaja was cleared of wrongdoing in the probe and announced his retirement in January.
Cricket Australia in 2018 imposed playing bans and other penalties on Smith, Warner and Bancroft. Head coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of direct involvement but resigned soon after the series.
Cricket Australia said on Saturday: "All relevant information presented to CA to date has been properly considered and we remain comfortable with the findings of our integrity process."
It added: "There has been the ongoing opportunity to present any relevant information, and this remains the case."
Australian captain Pat Cummins, one of the bowlers who played in the infamous test at Cape Town, this month dismissed suggestions that Khawaja’s autobiography could trigger further fallout when published.
South Africa won the 2018 four-match test series 3-1.
Australia's test team last month returned to South Africa for the first time since 2018 and lost the three-match series 2-1.

items.title: テニス＝ＷＴＡファイナル、練習の音声収録停止　選手の私的発言流出で
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［６日　ロイター］ - 女子テニス協会（ＷＴＡ）のバレリー・カミロ会長は６日、ＷＴＡファイナルの練習コートにおける音声録音機能を停止したと発表した。今週行われたライブ配信で選手の私的な発言が放送されてしまったことを受けた措置となる。

米カリフォルニア州インディアンウェルズで行われた練習セッションがＷＴＡのユーチューブチャンネルでライブ配信された際、ジェシカ・ペグラ（米国）とコーチの会話がマイクに拾われた。ペグラが、ロシア出身で今年の全仏オープン覇者であるミラ・アンドレエワを「ディーバ」と評し、「謙虚になる必要がある」などと述べた発言が交流サイト上で拡散された。

カミロ会長は録音に関する選手への掲示や事前通知が不十分だったことを認め、ＷＴＡファイナルでは練習コートでの音声録音は行わないとし、「周囲の音を拾おうとしたライブ配信が一定期間行われていたが、すでに修正されている。配信は削除された。大会期間中、練習コートでは今後、音声を録音しない」と記者団に語った。

ペグラは６日のメディア対応の場でこの件について質問されなかったが、米スポーツ専門局ＥＳＰＮに対し、「残念な事態」であるとコメント。選手のプライバシー保護の取り組みが推進されることを望んだ。

items.title: テニス＝アルカラスがマッチポイント2本しのぎ4強、マスターズ・パリ大会
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［パリ　６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［パリ　６日　ロイター］ - 男子テニスのマスターズ・パリ大会は６日、シングルス準々決勝を行い、第２シードのカルロス・アルカラス（スペイン）が第１１シードのテーラー・フリッツ（米国）に６─７、７─５、６─３で逆転勝ちし、初の４強入りを果たした。

アルカラスは第１セットで３本のセットポイントを逃し、タイブレークの末に先取された。第２セットも１─１から４本連続のブレークポイントをしのいだものの、その後にサービスゲームを落とし、３─４とリードを許した。その後、さらに２本のマッチポイントを握られる苦しい展開となったが、いずれもセーブして逆転。最終セットは序盤からリードを広げ、最初のマッチポイントで勝利を決めた。

フリッツはこの敗戦により１５日開幕のシーズン最終戦ＡＴＰファイナルへの出場を逃した。出場枠はラファエル・ホダル（スペイン）が獲得した。

第３シードのベン・シェルトンは第１２シードのトミー・ポールを６─４、４─６、６─３で下し、準決勝に進んだ。ポールは最終戦の出場権を逃し、フランシス・ティアフォー（いずれも米国）が出場を決めた。

そのほか、カスパー・ルード（ノルウェー）らが準決勝に進んだ。

items.body:
FIFA partially upholds AFA's appeal against post World Cup sanctions; Nahuel's suspension reduced As per Spanish newspaper Marca report quoted by Goal.com, FIFA cut the ban for Nahuel from seven matches to four and also reduced his fine from 90,000 dollars to 60,000. But for Parades, his 10-match suspension along with his 90,000 dollar fine still stands. 
ANI | Updated: 07-11-2026 14:41 IST | Created: 07-11-2026 14:41 IST

Argentina's Leandro Paredes clashed with Spain's Gavi after the match after Spain won the World Cup (Photo: Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

FIFA's Appeal Committee has partially upheld the Argentine Football Association (AFA) appeal against sanctions handed to several team members following the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, with Nahuel Molina's suspension getting reduced, while the punishment for midfielder Leandro Parades stands. As per a Spanish newspaper, Marca, report quoted by Goal.com, FIFA cut the ban for Nahuel from seven matches to four and also reduced his fine from 90,000 dollars to 60,000. But for Parades, his 10-match suspension along with his 90,000 dollar fine still stands.
In an official statement, the AFA said that they would be requesting the grounds for decisions before taking them to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS). AFA insists that they held "sufficient arguments from both a factual and legal standpoint" to demand a review of sanctions. Days after the World Cup final, the AFA was fined USD 321,000 for breaches of multiple articles of the FIFA Disciplinary Code (FDC), including the use of a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, discrimination and racist abuse, and failure to ensure order and security at matches, according to the statement issued by FIFA's Disciplinary Committee.
The sanctions were imposed in light of discriminatory chants and gestures by Argentina supporters during the tournament. In addition to the fine, the AFA was ordered to play its next two home matches with a limited number of spectators, allowing only 50 per cent attendance, due to the breach related to discrimination and racist abuse. FIFA further stated that USD 100,000 from the total fine must be invested in a plan aimed at combating discrimination. The governing body also confirmed that part of the sanction, including one of the two home-match restrictions and USD 100,000 of the fine, has been suspended with a probationary period.
Meanwhile, following the report submitted by the Disciplinary and Ethics Prosecutor regarding incidents during the FIFA World Cup 2026 final between Spain and Argentina, FIFA also announced individual sanctions. Argentina players Paredes and Nahuel Molina received suspensions of 10 and 7 matches, respectively, along with fines of USD 90,000 each. Thiago Almada has been handed a one-match suspension and fined USD 30,000, while team official Roberto Ayala has been suspended for three matches and fined USD 30,000. Paredes, the Argentine midfielder, was involved in a post-match ruckus after Argentina's loss to Spain courtesy of an extra-time winner from Ferran Torres.
Spain player Pablo Martin Paez Gavira also received a one-match suspension and a fine of USD 30,000. (ANI)

items.title: サッカー＝アーセナルのサカ、負傷で数週間離脱へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［６日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグ、アーセナルのミケル・アルテタ監督は６日、太ももの筋肉を負傷したイングランド代表ＦＷブカヨ・サカ（２５）が数週間離脱する見通しを示した。

サカは先月行われた欧州チャンピオンズリーグ（ＣＬ）のバイエルン・ミュンヘン（ドイツ）戦で大腿四頭筋を負傷。今月の欧州ネーションズリーグ（ＮＬ）のクロアチア戦とスペイン戦も欠場する。

アルテタ監督は報道陣に対し、「（離脱は）数週間という話になる。代表戦による中断期間が終われば、練習を再開できるだろう。ただ、残念ながらしばらくは離脱することになる」と説明した。

一方、４日に行われたＣＬのスラビア・プラハ（チェコ）戦で膝に違和感を覚えて途中交代したＤＦエズリ・コンサについては、状態が改善していると明かした。

アーセナルはプレミアリーグで９試合を終えて勝ち点２４の首位。欧州ＣＬでもパリ・サンジェルマン（フランス）、レアル・マドリード（スペイン）と勝ち点２差の３位につけている。

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝ドジャース、ベイツ打撃コーチが退団へ　新契約で合意に至らず
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［６日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）のドジャースがアーロン・ベイツ打撃コーチ（４２）と契約を更新せず、同コーチが退団する見通しとなった。複数の米メディアが６日に報じた。球団との新契約交渉で合意に至らなかったという。

ベイツ氏は２００６年のドラフト３巡目でレッドソックスに指名され、０９年にメジャーで５試合に出場。１４年を最後に現役を退いた後、１５年からドジャース傘下で指導者としてのキャリアを開始した。１９年にメジャーの打撃コーチ補佐に就任し、２３年から共同打撃コーチを務めていた。

ドジャースは２５年、２６年ともにシーズン後半に打線が低迷。今季はオールスター戦後の得点が２９５でメジャー１１位、本塁打も７７本で同１１位だった。

球団は２年連続でワールドシリーズを制した後、今季はナ・リーグ地区シリーズでブレーブスを破ったものの、リーグ優勝決定シリーズではブルワーズに４連敗を喫した。

一方、ドジャースは今季のナ・リーグ最優秀攻撃チームに贈られるシルバースラッガー賞の最終候補に選ばれている。１７日に受賞チームが発表される。

items.body:
［アスンシオン　６日　ロイター］ - 南米パラグアイで６日、アリアナ新大統領が就任宣誓した。当局は弾劾で罷免されたペニャ前大統領を自宅軟禁下に置いた。デジタル銀行「ウエノバンク」が破綻し、同国の人口約６５０万人の半分弱に当たる約３００万人の預金者が銀行口座を利用できなくなったことで、ペニャ政権への抗議活動が広がっていた。

首都アスンシオンのペニャ氏の自宅前で取材に応じた検察当局者は、容疑の内容はなお精査中だが、影響力の不正行使が含まれる可能性があると述べた。 ペニャ氏は７日午前に検察庁に出頭するよう命じられた。

下院は５日、臨時議会でペニャ氏の弾劾訴追案を可決。上院も６日、全会一致でペニャ氏の罷免を決定した。議員らは、破綻したデジタル銀行と同氏の過去の関係に疑義があると指摘した。

ペニャ氏は５日に辞意を表明したが、上院は辞任を受け入れるのではなく、弾劾手続きを完了させることを選択。速やかにアリアナ副大統領を後任に据えた。

アスンシオン中心部にはデモ参加者が押し寄せ、デジタル銀行破綻の責任追及や、凍結された預金の迅速な払い戻しを要求。「われわれの金を返せ」などと声を上げた。

items.body:
"Some things are best left unsaid": Darren Lehmann after Khawaja's explosive 2018 ball-tampering scandal claims Khawaja has claimed that the entire Australian team, including players and support staff, was involved in the 2018 ball-tampering scandal during the South Africa tour.  He said the responsibility was collective, contrary to Cricket Australia's findings that implicated only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft. Khawaja stressed that he had expected the truth to emerge over the past eight years and spoke out to ensure the three players were not left carrying the blame alone.

Usman Khawaja. (Photo: Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Former Australian head coach Darren Lehmann questioned former batter Usman Khawaja's bombshell revelations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying that "somethings are best left unsaid sometimes for the good of the game and people". Khawaja has claimed that the entire Australian team, including players and support staff, was involved in the 2018 ball-tampering scandal during the South Africa tour.  He said the responsibility was collective, contrary to Cricket Australia's findings that implicated only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft. Khawaja stressed that he had expected the truth to emerge over the past eight years and spoke out to ensure the three players were not left carrying the blame alone.
Until now, the widely accepted account of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, maintained by Cricket Australia (CA) and those involved, was that Steven Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were the only players responsible. Smith and Warner received 12-month bans from international and domestic cricket, while Bancroft was handed a nine-month suspension. Lehmann, who resigned from his position as head coach after the Sandpaper-Gate scandal, spoke on ABC Grandstand on Saturday after Khawaja's explosive claims about the whole team knowing the fact that a sandpaper had been used during the Cape Town Test in March 2018.
"It has been an eventful morning, has not it? It just brings back really bad memories. It was a bad day in Australian cricket,” Lehmann said. “Everyone around the world was doing it, as people have spoken about. The extent of how much everyone knew, that is an individual case by case. For the families and the people involved, I feel for them right now because it is taking them back to a really bad place. It is a tough one, mate. It is not ideal at the start of the summer."
“It is eight years ago, so some of the things you remember, some you do not," he added. Lehmann suggested that "some things were best left unsaid" as Khawaja made these revelations ahead of release of his autobiography titled 'Sabr' on Tuesday. He questioned if Khawaja could have said those things way back then.
"Could he [Khawaja] have said this at the time [eight years]? I suppose that is one of the things in the book. Books are there to sell. He is retired. I have not spoken to Usman, to be fair. He has not texted me or rung me. That is just the way it is," he said. "I had to have a lot of help ... behind the scenes [after that incident]. It is not easy to talk about … but it puts you back in a bad place. Hopefully, I can get through this."
"That is part and parcel of selling books, I suppose. I do not know what he is getting paid. He is probably getting paid a lot of money to do it. Is it worth it? I do not know. Maybe I write a book. Sometimes things are [best] left unsaid sometimes for the good of the game, and the good of the people," he continued. Asked on if the left-handed batter called for the team to take a collective responsibility after the scandal, Lehmann said that he dos not remember Khawaja doing so.
"No, I do not remember that,” Lehmann said. “There were two change rooms [at the Cape Town venue] and meetings going on everywhere. I was in meetings with Cricket Australia a lot. I cannot remember that, but it could have been the case. That is what it is from his point of view," he said. “I do not think everyone would have known. But you do know ball tampering is going on because it has been happening for 150 years," he added.
Lehmann also said that it is now upto the pace trio of Mitchell Starc, skipper Pat Cummins and Josh Hazlewood and spinner Nathan Lyon to speak to Khawaja. The revelations have renewed some scrutiny around these bowlers, who issued a joint statement back in 2021 denying that they were aware of a foreign substance being present on the field to alter the ball's conditions. "How much did they know? Only they know individually. They have been greats of the game. We are talking eight years ago. It is the Australian captain (Cummins). He has done a bloody good job over a long period of time," he signed off.
Coming to Khawaja's statements, the southpaw had said to Nine as per Cricinfo, "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us. In an ideal world, I don't want to do this. I don't want to be the one who comes out and talks about the truth. The issue is that I genuinely thought after eight years the truth would have been out by now." "Maybe I thought Davey would have exposed it, or someone else would have talked about it more. I just didn't think it was going to come down to this. But the longer it is gone on for, and right from the very start, I have been on the train of collectively taking it," he added.
Khawaja said he had urged the Australian team to take collective responsibility for the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, insisting that everyone knew what was happening. He expressed disappointment that Smith, Warner and Bancroft were left to shoulder the blame, adding that Warner had faced repeated criticism over the past eight years while remaining silent. "Even in the change rooms when I was talking to them after the game. I said, 'Take this as a team'. We did this as a team. We knew what was going on, and we had to take it as a team, and so I was always of that stance. Obviously, it didn't work that way, and those three guys got crucified. I have seen Davey over the last eight years just get nailed bad over and over again, and it's taken a big man not to say anything and just to stay quiet," Khawaja added.
Khawaja highlighted the lasting impact of the 2018 scandal on Cameron Bancroft and Steve Smith. He noted that Bancroft has struggled to regain his place in the Test side despite consistently scoring runs, while Smith successfully rebuilt his career but has never forgotten the events of that year. "And then 'Bangers' [Bancroft], in the same note, particularly, he played a little bit of Test cricket after that, but then never came back in, even though he's been scoring a lot of runs. He's been a terrific cricketer for a long time, but I know it's something that hangs over his head," Khawaja said.
"Even Steve Smith. Steve's lucky, the greatest batsman of my generation. He came back from that, and he is come back as good as he ever was in that first Ashes series, and it is kind of been forgotten for him in some respects. But I know he has never forgotten that year and how it all panned out," he added. Khawaja said he spoke out because he believed Smith, Warner and Bancroft deserved justice and should not continue bearing the blame alone. He added that none of the three wanted to break their silence, fearing their accounts would be dismissed as hearsay, which prompted him to speak on their behalf.
"But I am not doing this for any other reason than I think it is the right thing to do. I have always felt like there is more to life than just cricket, and these guys, in some respect, deserve that justice. And it just does not feel like anyone's going to give it to them. None of those three wants to be the first to say anything. And rightly so, it will just be hearsay and 'their word' if they do. They needed someone else to say something," he said. Khawaja also revealed that Cricket Australia never interviewed him during its investigation into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. The probe, led by then head of integrity Iain Roy and team performance manager Pat Howard, followed the Cape Town Test and resulted in sanctions against Smith, Warner and Bancroft.
"I was sitting next to Cam Bancroft that whole Test match, and I didn't get interviewed. I thoroughly feel that I didn't get interviewed because of that, because they knew that I wanted to take it as a team, because they knew I was ready to tell the truth if I was interviewed," he concluded. (ANI)

items.title: Ｆ１＝ブラジルＧＰフリー走行、王者アントネッリがトップ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［サンパウロ　６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［サンパウロ　６日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１の今季第２０戦、ブラジル・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は６日、サンパウロでフリー走行２回を行い、メルセデスのキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア）がこの日のトップタイムを記録した。

アントネッリは２回目で最速１分１０秒７６３をマーク。０秒２５３差でマクラーレンのランド・ノリス（英国）が続いた。ノリスは１回目の最速１分１１秒７１７を記録していた。

３番手にアントネッリと０秒２５９差でレッドブルのマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ）が入った。メルセデスのジョージ・ラッセル（英国）が４番手、マクラーレンのオスカー・ピアストリ（オーストラリア）が５番手で続いた。

先週末のメキシコＧＰで３位に入って史上最年少で個人総合優勝を決めたアントネッリは「まだ取り組むべきことはあるが、全体的な感触は良いし、明日が楽しみ。良いチャンスがあると思う」と語った。

メルセデスはブラジルＧＰでフェラーリを３ポイント以上上回れば、コンストラクターズ部門のタイトルを確定することができる。

items.summary: US President Donald Trump dismissed the ongoing conflict with Iran as "not a war", claiming significant progress and increased oil extraction. While defending past strikes against Iran's nuclear ...
items.body:
"Nobody hurt or killed in 5 months": Trump says US is not at war with Iran US President Donald Trump dismissed the ongoing conflict with Iran as "not a war", claiming significant progress and increased oil extraction. While defending past strikes against Iran's nuclear infrastructure, reports indicate that the true damage remains unclear, and Tehran maintains that its nuclear programme is peaceful.
ANI | Updated: 07-11-2026 13:33 IST | Created: 07-11-2026 13:33 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters) . Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump has described the ongoing confrontation with Iran as "not a war", claiming that Washington has made significant progress in dealing with Tehran and is currently extracting more oil than before the hostilities. "We made a lot of progress with Iran. We’re taking out more oil now than we were before the war. It’s not a war. It can’t be a war when for five months nobody was hurt, killed, or anything else. It’s not a war," Donald Trump said.
These assertions come amid persistent ambiguity regarding the trajectory of the US military campaign targeting Iran, alongside ongoing deliberations concerning fresh air strikes. His contention that current tensions do not constitute a war persists despite White House deliberations regarding active military options, while broader friction with Tehran remains a primary regional concern. Furthermore, the American leader asserted that regional stability depended entirely on his administration's past interventions to obstruct Iranian atomic development. In a statement disseminated through his Truth Social platform, Donald Trump stated that his personal intervention against Iran’s nuclear ambitions remained universally recognised yet deliberately underreported.
"Israel and, in fact, the entire Middle East, WOULD NOT EXIST TODAY if I did not stop Iran from having a Nuclear Weapon. Nobody wants to say that, but everybody knows it’s true!" he wrote. Trump has repeatedly portrayed operations directed at Iran’s nuclear infrastructure as an unqualified triumph. Both Washington and Israeli forces carried out extensive bombardments targeting Iranian nuclear and military facilities across 2025 and 2026, framing deterrence against the acquisition of atomic weapons as their core objective.
Nevertheless, a full assessment of the damage sustained by Tehran's atomic enterprise remains inconclusive. A Congressional Research Service assessment published in October highlighted that the precise operational impact on indigenous weapons manufacturing capability remains undefined. The evaluation additionally emphasised past intelligence consensus indicating that Tehran had refrained from constructing atomic devices. Meanwhile, Iranian authorities persistently refute ambitions concerning nuclear weapons development, asserting that exclusively civilian applications govern their domestic atomic framework. (ANI)

items.title: ゴルフ＝ＴＯＴＯジャパンクラシック、畑岡が単独首位に浮上
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［６日　ロイター］ - 女子ゴルフで日米の両ツアーを兼ねるＴＯＴＯジャパンクラシックは６日、茨城県の太平洋クラブ美野里（パー７２）で第２ラウンドを行い、昨年覇者の畑岡奈紗が６４をマークし、通算１２アンダーの１３２で単独首位に浮上した。

前日７位の畑岡は１イーグル、８バーディー、２ボギーの成績。１７番でイーグルを奪うなど後半９ホールを３０で回り、大会連覇に向けて好位置につけた。

首位で出た山下美夢有は６バーディー、１ボギーの６７で回り、通算１１アンダーの２位。前週の米ツアーで今季３勝目を挙げた山下は２週連続優勝を狙う。

菅楓華は通算１０アンダーの３位。原英莉花、佐久間朱莉、河本結、岩井明愛、高橋彩華が９アンダーの５位で続いた。

渋野日向子は７１で回り、通算３オーバーの７２位となった。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［６日　ロイター］ - サッカーのドイツ１部ブンデスリーガは６日、１試合を行い、日本人３選手が先発したボルシアＭＧは敵地でハンブルガーＳＶに１─３で敗れた。

板倉滉、宇野禅斗、町野修斗が先発したボルシアＭＧは前半１１分に先制を許したが、同４４分にジョー・スカリーが同点弾をマーク。しかし後半４分、板倉が抜け出した相手を引っ張り、この日２枚目のイエローカードを受けて退場した。

数的不利となったボルシアＭＧは、その後に２失点。チームは今季７敗目で、勝ち点４の最下位と苦しんでいる。宇野と町野はともに後半３６分までプレー、チームメートの橋岡大樹はメンバー外だった。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［６日　ロイター］ - フィギュアスケートのグランプリ（ＧＰ）シリーズ第３戦、中国杯は６日、中国の深センで開幕し、男子ショートプログラム（ＳＰ）では三浦佳生が１０２．９０点、女子は千葉百音が７６．０８点でそれぞれ首位に立った。

三浦は冒頭の４回転サルコーと３回転トーループの連続ジャンプを決めると、トリプルアクセル（３回転半ジャンプ）、演技後半の４回転トーループも成功。ステップでは最高難度のレベル４を獲得した。

佐藤駿が１０１．９７点で２位につけ、日本勢が上位２位を占めた。佐藤は冒頭の４回転ルッツ、続く４回転トーループと３回転トーループの連続ジャンプを成功させ、後半のトリプルアクセルも決めた。

女子では千葉が冒頭の３回転フリップと３回転トーループの連続ジャンプを成功させ、演技後半の３回転ルッツでも加点を獲得。ステップと３種類のスピンはいずれもレベル４の評価を受けた。

Nov 6 : SpaceX disclosed on Friday that Google executive Donald Harrison has resigned from the rockets-to-AI company's board after more than a decade.
Here are some details:

• The Elon Musk-led company said Harrison's decision to resign was not due to any disagreement with the company on matters relating to its operations, policies or practices

items.title: Noel Tata to step down as Voltas chairman, appointed Chairman Emeritus
items.summary: Noel N Tata, Chairman of Tata Trusts, has been appointed as Chairman Emeritus of Voltas, a day after he retired as Chairman and Director of the leading cooling products maker.
items.body:
Home / Companies / News / Noel Tata to step down as Voltas chairman, appointed Chairman Emeritus

Noel Tata to step down as Voltas chairman, appointed Chairman Emeritus Noel Tata retired as Voltas chairman and director on November 11 upon reaching the age of superannuation

Noel Tata, who was born on November 12, 1956, will turn 70 on November 12, 2026 (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 07 2026 | 12:51 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Noel N Tata, Chairman of Tata Trusts, has been appointed as Chairman Emeritus of Voltas, a day after he retired as Chairman and Director of the leading cooling products maker.
Noel Tata will retire as Chairman and Director of Voltas Ltd on November 11, 2026, upon attaining the age of superannuation under Tata Group governance guidelines.
Following his retirement, "the Board has appointed him as Chairman Emeritus of the Company with effect from November 12, 2026," said Voltas, a Tata Group firm, in its regulatory filing.
The Companies Act 2013 mandates that any managing director or whole-time director cannot be appointed or continue employment if they are 70 years of age or older.
 

Noel Tata, who was born on November 12, 1956, will turn 70 on November 12, 2026. He has been associated with Voltas since 2003.
Also Read

Additionally, the board has appointed Sunil D'Souza as the new Chairman of Voltas.
D'Souza currently leads the Tata Group's FMCG arm, Tata Consumer Products Ltd (TCPL), as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer. The company sells a wide range of consumer products, including salt, tea, coffee, packaged foods and beverages under brands such as Tata Salt, Tata Tea, Tetley and Tata Sampann.
"The Board has appointed Sunil Alaric D'Souza as Chairman of the Company with effect from November 12, 2026," Voltas said.

Moreover, the tenure of Voltas Managing Director C P Mukundan Menon will end on May 24, 2027, when he will retire from the company's services in line with the Tata Group's retirement policy for executive directors.
The board has approved the appointment of Jayant Balan, currently Head of the Room Air Conditioner Business, as an Additional Director and Managing Director for a five-year term beginning May 25, 2027, subject to shareholders' approval.
"As part of a planned succession process, the Board, based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, has approved the appointment of Jayant Balan, currently Head - Room Air Conditioner Business, as an Additional Director and Managing Director of the Company for a term of five years commencing from May 25, 2027," Voltas said.

This will be subject to the approval of the shareholders.
To ensure a smooth transition, Balan has been redesignated as Head Room Air Conditioner Business and Managing Director Designate until his appointment takes effect.
The board has also approved the appointment of Venkatesalu Palaniswamy as an Additional Director in the non-independent, non-executive category with effect from November 12, 2026.
